items.description: Job 1: TradingView Auto-Trendline & Alert System (Step 1) Project Overview: I am looking for a developer to build an automatic trendline indicator in TradingView (Pine Script) that automatically draws trendlines and triggers alerts based on specific price-action rules. This is Step 1 of a larger automated trading project. Core Requirements: * Automatically detect and draw upward and downward trendlines on the chart. * Generate accurate email alerts based on the following strict logic: * Downward Trendline (Drawn Top to Bottom): * Bounce: When price moves from bottom to top and touches the trendline \rightarrow Trigger SELL alert. * Breakout: If the price crosses the trendline and the candle closes above it \rightarrow Trigger BUY alert. * Upward Trendline (Drawn Bottom to Top): * Bounce: When price moves from top to bottom and touches the trendline \rightarrow Trigger BUY alert. * Breakdown: If the price crosses the trendline and the candle closes below it \rightarrow Trigger SELL alert. Strict Payment Terms: * This is Step 1 of a two-part project. No upfront payments or partial milestones will be released. 100% of the payment will be released only after the entire project (both Step 1 and Step 2) is fully completed, delivered, and successfully tested. Core Requirements: * Email-to-MT4 Bridge: Develop or set up a script/tool that reads TradingView email alerts and instantly forwards the execution commands to MT4. * MT4 EA Execution: The MT4 Expert Advisor must automatically open and close trades 24/7 on my local PC based on the received email signals. * No Limitations: The system must be capable of processing signals from unlimited trendlines across any timeframe simultaneously. items.description: We are looking for a developer to build a standalone Windows application (developed in C# .NET or C++) that acts as an automated controller for a third-party graphical Win32 process. The integration must be handled via direct RAM reading (Memory Reading / ReadProcessMemory / dynamic offset scanning). Important: Solutions based on screen clickers, macro recorders, or image recognition (e.g., OpenCV) will not be considered. We require strict data analytics retrieved directly from RAM. Key Functionality: 1. Memory Reading & Navigation: The application must read a specific data structure (a 2D coordinate map of passability and objects positioned on it) from the process's address space. Based on this dynamic data, the application must calculate optimal travel routes using the A* (A-Star) algorithm, complete with anti-stuck logic. 2. Rapid Response Module (State Machine): Continuous monitoring of specific triggers in memory. If a numerical value drops below a critical threshold (e.g., <35%), the application must instantly execute an emergency action: either a forced TCP Disconnect (severing the process's network connection) or killing the process with zero delay. 3. Input Emulation: Based on the calculated coordinates, the program must emulate mouse and keyboard actions (via WinAPI / SendInput / driver-level emulation) with configurable timing randomization (Humanizer logic) to mimic natural user behavior. 4. Cyclic Data & Inventory Management: When a specific buffer or inventory fills up, the program must execute a routine to return to the starting point and organize objects using Ctrl+Click emulation. items.description: Helpdesk Automation: Business Requirements Nov 4, 2026 · Fatai This document defines two automated request types: Pepperi credential requests and new SAP user creation. Any other request goes to the L1 helpdesk. 1. Scope In scope • Credential requests (login, password, or access) for an existing Pepperi account. • New SAP user creation, requested from the SAP Accounting team by email. Out of scope • Other software, hardware, and access requests. • Elevated or admin roles. • SAP role assignment and job-title mapping. • Creating Pepperi accounts. • Any task the helpdesk has not delegated to the automation. 2. Intake • Trigger: an email from Spiceworks for a new ticket. There is no polling. • Required ticket fields: ticket number, requester name and email, summary, description, category, and ticket type. • The requester must be an employee on an allowed domain: gmfoods.com, ziyad.com, globalchoicefoods.com, or pepperi.com (see open item 4). • If a required field is missing, email the requester for it. 3. Classification • Credential request: asks for a login, password, or access to an existing Pepperi account. • New user request: asks for a new SAP user. • Anything else, or anything unclear: route to the helpdesk. 4. Workflow 1: Credential request Inputs: the Pepperi account ID and username from the ticket, and the requester's email address. 1. Look up the credential in the data source (open item 1), using the ticket parameters. 2. If the lookup finds no match, route to the helpdesk. If it finds more than one match, email the requester to confirm the account, then wait for the reply. 3. Email the credential to the requester. 4. Update the ticket and write the audit record. Credential values are never written to the ticket or the audit record. 5. Workflow 2: New user creation (SAP) Required: email address (unique ID) and store name. SAP accepts only these two for a new account. 1. Check that both required fields are present. If either is missing, email the requester for it. 2. Check that the requester is a Business Manager or GM Foods employee. If not, route to the helpdesk. 3. Get Accounting Manager approval, by reply or approval record. 4. Search SAP by store name and email address. If a match exists, route to the helpdesk. 5. Email the SAP Accounting team to create the user, with the user's email address and the store name. 6. When the Accounting team confirms creation, email the result to the requester with the Business Manager in CC. Then update the ticket

items.description: Technical Work Specification & Scope of Work Project Title: Automation, PLC Logic Programming, and HMI Screen Development for -70°C Cascade Cooling Environmental Test Chamber 1. System Overview & Hardware Architecture The supplier/programmer is required to develop, test, and commission the complete automation logic and HMI interface for a specialized -70°C multi-stage cascade refrigeration environmental test chamber. PLC Hardware: Delta DVP-16SS2 main CPU, DVP08SN (SN08) digital output expansion module, DVP04AD-S analog input module, and DVP04PT-S RTD temperature input module. HMI Hardware: Flexem 7000 Series HMI (FE7000 / FE7300) communicating via RS-485 Modbus RTU (COM1 port, 9600 baud, 7 data bits, Even parity, 1 stop bit). 2. Scope of PLC Programming (WPLSoft) Analog Data Acquisition: Configure FROM/TO instructions to read PT100 Class A temperature sensors (Chamber live temperature D100, specimen safety temperature D102, and refrigeration coil temperature D104) along with analog pressure transmitters and humidity sensors (D110 to D115). Compressor Cascade Sequencing & Interlocks: Implement master safety interlocks (M0 derived from emergency stops, door switches X2, and water/airflow flow switches X3). Program a 2-minute equalization timer (T0) and strict sequence interlocks ensuring the Higher Side compressor starts first, followed by the Lower Side compressor based on discharge/suction pressure feedback and safety trips (M101, M103). Control multiple solenoid bypass valves (Y13 to Y17) and the main liquid line solenoid valve (Y20). PID Heating & PWM Control: Implement standard PID instruction loop using chamber temperature (D100), target setpoint (D20), and tuning registers (D200–D203), coupled with GPWM output instruction to drive the booster solid-state relay heater (Y7). 3. Scope of HMI Programming (Flexem FStudio) Dashboard & Navigation: Design an intuitive multi-screen HMI application including a Home Dashboard, P&ID Refrigeration Circuit screen, Timer/Parameter Settings page, and Alarm/Trend screen. Tag Mapping & Controls: Configure numeric displays for live temperatures and pressure transmitters (D100–D115), numeric entry fields for temperature setpoint (D20) and equalization time delay (D220), maintained bit switches for system start/stop (M10), and multi-state indicator lamps for compressors (Y3, Y4), blowers (Y6), and solenoid valves. 4. Deliverables & Acceptance Criteria Fully compiled and error-free WPLSoft ladder logic file (.wpl / .gxw).

No browser automation, no desktop-app tricks—pure API calls. How it should work • I paste or load the list of customer phone numbers (all are existing contacts). • I type a free-form message in a memo field. • When I hit Send, the program calls the /messages endpoint, passes the numbers one by one (or in a batch if that is allowed), and returns the WhatsApp message IDs so I can see delivery and read status. • Any API errors (rate limits, bad tokens, etc.) must be caught and shown in a log panel and written to a lightweight SQLite file for auditing. Technical preferences • Delphi 11 or higher, using native REST components or a lightweight HTTP library. • JSON handling via System.JSON or SuperObject—whatever is cleanest. • Bearer token and phone-number-ID should be loaded from an .ini file so I can update credentials without recompiling. Deliverables 1. Compiled Windows 64-bit executable. 2. Full, well-commented Delphi source code. 3. README explaining how to obtain the WhatsApp Business access token, where to place it, and how to run the program. 4. Quick test demonstrating a successful send and retrieval of delivery status. Acceptance criteria The build is considered complete when I can: • Enter a text string, choose at least one existing customer number, click Send, and see the message appear in the customer’s chat. • Refresh status and view “sent”, “delivered”, or “read” inside the app. • Restart the program and find the same event logged in SQLite. If you have already worked with the WhatsApp Business or Cloud API in Delphi (or even in another language you can port), please mention it—experience here matters more than general messaging know-how.
